original_source_topology.quantifiers: All real r in the Appendix B results. Every finite p>=1 satisfying (-r-t)*p.toReal>1 in fixed-exponent statements; literal existential statements also require t<-r and use the uniform witness t=-r-2,p=1. Boundedness is derived for convergent sequences and compact sets; no global bounded-range claim is made for arbitrary convergent nets.

results: The original physical endpoint norm is weak-star lower semicontinuous. Any specified bound is retained under weak-star closure and under limits of eventually bounded nets.

A lower finite-p norm limit of eventually endpoint-bounded original physical potentials is the identical lower distribution of an endpoint potential with the same norm bound and all physical conditions.

For bounded original physical source sets, ambient closure consists exactly of sequential limits within the set; ambient weak-star closedness can be checked with sequences. Maps out of such bounded sets are continuous iff sequentially continuous.
One physical weak-star subsequence converges in every admissible original lower finite-p norm space, with the subsequence chosen before the exponents.
Continuity into bounded physical sets can be tested using all original Fourier coefficients or any admissible lower norm realization.

Arbitrary-filter compact-open weak-star trajectory convergence equals uniform lower norm convergence on every compact time set. On compact domains it has the explicit single-eventual-error-bound-for-all-times criterion.

On bounded physical initial-data sets, sequential uniform lower norm dependence suffices for continuity into the full compact-time weak-star trajectory space. In the article range the lower norm can be the identical original H-minus-one norm.
bounded_physical_limits_and_trajectory_c.qualifications: Sequential closure and continuity criteria require endpoint norm-bounded source sets. Limit-bound statements for arbitrary filters require a nontrivial filter; uniform compact-time criteria retain a common endpoint-bounded target. No global bounded-range assertion is made for arbitrary convergent nets. All lower exponents retain the exact strict finite-p threshold.

results: Arbitrary-filter weak-star convergence of norm-bounded original physical families is equivalent to convergence of every original Fourier coefficient and to convergence in each admissible original lower finite-p norm.

Both convergence criteria remain valid under only an eventual specified endpoint norm bound. No global bounded-range or eventual-boundedness conclusion is claimed for arbitrary weak-star convergent nets.

Pointwise Fourier limits of eventually endpoint-bounded nets uniquely represent an original real mean-zero period-one endpoint potential with the same bound, and the entire net converges weak-star to it.

A lower finite-p norm limit of an eventually endpoint-bounded net uniquely recovers the identical original physical endpoint distribution, preserves the specified bound and gives convergence of the entire net. In the article range this applies directly to the original H-minus-one norm.
eventually_bounded_physical_nets.qualifications: Topology equivalences accept arbitrary filters, assuming eventual membership in a specified original endpoint norm ball. Existence and specified-bound retention require a nontrivial filter. All lower norm exponents satisfy finite p>=1 and (-r-t)*p.toReal>1. Weak-star convergence alone is not asserted to imply eventual endpoint norm boundedness.

results: Weak-star closure is compact iff the original physical endpoint norm is bounded; the same equivalence holds for sequential compactness of the closure.

Every original Fourier coefficient is continuous on the full physical weak-star space. Any family of closed coefficient constraints is weak-star closed, and its intersection with a specified original endpoint norm ball is compact.

Every closed endpoint-bounded physical set is a closed embedding into each admissible original lower finite-p norm space. In particular the original endpoint norm ball has a closed lower-norm image, with its weak-star topology retained.

A sequence in a specified original norm ball satisfying arbitrary closed Fourier constraints has a strictly increasing subsequence whose original physical limit retains both the same norm bound and all constraints. That single subsequence converges in every admissible lower finite-p original distribution norm.
